docs.title: Canvas cannot see Lab Tools
docs.text:
• Studio → Manage → Integrations: does Lab Tools Production (Tenant) show Configured? If it shows Configure, select it and paste your seat token.
  • Canvas → Integrations → Custom Integrations: does Lab Tools Production show Your credential: Saved and Enabled for me ticked?
  • Start a new board after adding the credential; an open board may not pick it up.
  • Name it in your prompt: "Using Lab Tools Production, …". If Canvas also lists an older Lab Tools, it may try that one first and be refused; that is harmless.

docs.title: Canvas looks at Hyperfabric (USC-HF-LEAF1/2) instead of the Meraki Cloud Fabric
docs.text: Canvas did not get the PseudoCo environment reference, which comes with Lab Tools Production. Check that it is Enabled for me with your credential saved (above), start a new board, and ask again. You can also say it outright: "the Meraki Cloud Fabric, org USC-Engineering, network SITE-105".

docs.title: "missing or invalid bearer token" (401)
docs.text:
Your seat token was mistyped, has a trailing space, or belongs to an earlier session (tokens change between sessions). Copy it again from your seat card, then update the credential:

  • Studio: Manage → Integrations → Lab Tools Production → ⋯ → Update credential (Canvas uses the same one).
  • Your own 2.3 integration, if you built one: Manage → Integrations → it → ⋯ → Update credential.

docs.title: "rate limit" (429)
docs.text: Your token made more than 30 calls in a minute, usually an agent stuck in a loop. Wait a minute and check the agent's instructions for a step it repeats.

docs.title: Studio says "Agent update needs attention: The Agent could not be prepared"
docs.text: Studio's web firewall blocks any message that looks like a web attack, for example text with ../ paths, SQL injection strings or scanner names, so Studio never receives it. Length is not the problem. Describe attacks in plain words ("unusual web request paths, web scanner user agents") instead of quoting attack strings, then start the agent again from Build → Agent. Do not paste raw firewall events or sample URLs into Studio chat. Check Studio → Manage first: a failed attempt does not create an agent.

docs.title: "Schedule failed: Your user identity is unavailable. Sign in again."
docs.text: Your Cloud Control session expired while the builder was open, so Studio cannot say who owns the schedule. Nothing was scheduled. Reload the page (sign in again if asked), open Schedule again and choose the next 5-minute slot that is at least 5 minutes away: the dialog forgets your earlier choices.

docs.title: A run says a tool "returned HTTP 503"
docs.text: Your Path B workspace server (My Lab Tools - MCP) is not running, for example after a proctor reset. The agent may fall back to Lab Tools Production for the alert, and the report then names the wrong integration. Open your MCP workspace (the link on your seat card), select Save (or Restart), and check that Test a tool answers again. Path A students never see this.

docs.title: Studio discovers fewer than 10 tools
docs.text: Use ⋯ → Rediscover on the integration (it asks for your token again). If the URL is not the one on your seat card, edit the integration.

docs.title: My tile will not turn green
docs.text: clear_issue only clears your seat, and your agent calls it only when the last 5 minutes of your source are quiet and your lane is stopped. Events reach Splunk a minute or two late, so wait two minutes after the stop and run the check again. get_light_status shows whether your alert is still open.

docs.title: The agent says my lane is stopped, but events continue
docs.text: Events reach Splunk a minute or two late. Wait two minutes and check again with a short window (minutes=5). If events still arrive, call stop_my_lane again (it is safe to repeat) and tell a proctor.

docs.title: Canvas shows "There is an issue connecting to this canvas"
docs.text: The chat reconnects by itself. If the answer seems to disappear, reload the page; finished answers are kept on the board.

docs.title: A caution sign next to my agent ("stale skills")
docs.text:
In Studio → Manage → Applications, a caution sign next to your agent opens Products with stale skills and names an integration (for example your own My Lab Tools - MCP). Studio's cached copy of that integration's tools is out of date, which happens after the server behind it changed.

Fix: Studio → Manage → Integrations → the named integration → ⋯ → Rediscover, paste your seat token, Rediscover tools. The caution sign clears for every agent that uses it. Asking the agent's Studio chat to "refresh skills" does not help: the skills belong to the integration, not the agent. Your agent kept working the whole time; run its test again afterwards anyway.

docs.title: My tickets says "That token was not accepted"
docs.text: Open it again with Log in to Service Desk on your seat card (it passes your token for you), or paste the seat token from the card. After the proctor rotates tokens between sessions, old tokens stop working on purpose.

docs.title: Canvas or my agent cannot see PseudoCo Service Desk
docs.text: Check Studio → Manage → Integrations → PseudoCo Service Desk shows Configured, and in Canvas → Integrations → Custom Integrations that it shows Your credential: Saved and Enabled for me. In the agent, ask Studio to "add my integration PseudoCo Service Desk", then rerun a test.

docs.title: The agent answers "duplicate: true" when it opens a ticket
docs.text: That is the Service Desk protecting you: an open ticket already covers the same service, so no second one was opened. The agent should work the ticket it returns. If it keeps calling create_incident, add to its instructions: "List open tickets first; open a ticket only when none covers the issue."

docs.title: "Only the caller closes a ticket" (403)
docs.text: The agent tried to close a ticket. It can only resolve it (with close_code and close_notes); you close it on My tickets. Remove any "close the ticket" wording from its instructions.

docs.title: There is no ticket in my queue
docs.text: Part 1 tickets arrive about 2 minutes after the proctor breaks the branch network; Lights Out tickets arrive when the proctor opens them at the start of 2.5. If yours is still missing after that, ask a proctor: they can open one for your seat only.

docs.title: Mission Control says "No night recorded yet" (or only "Attack started")
docs.text: The app shows only the night since your attack last started. Restarting your lane (Restart my lane, Start my traffic, or Run it live again) or a proctor reset starts a new, empty night. Make sure your lane is running, then trigger your agent (Test in Studio, or its next scheduled slot). When your card turns Resolved, the timeline, response times, tickets and Replay the night fill in. Tickets stay in your queue either way: the Tickets panel still lists them.
